To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(1) patients with schizophrenia show an excessive sense of agency, (2) this is associated with the strength of their positive symptoms and (3) it is reflected in the motor system, in the form of a greater interference between the two hands when observing the examiner’s movements.

(a) patients with schizophrenia have a sense of agency altered towards the excessive attribution of actions to the self, as internally generated, rather than externally; and (b), this altered sense of agency can have objective consequences on motor system, inducing an interference effect on the own motor action, when observing the examiner’s movements.

the sense of agency is altered in patients with schizophrenia and that this alteration can be objectively observed by means of a bimanual coupling paradigm.
